title: The excretory system
log: 2026-11-01T08:04:31Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: The bank point is about vision correction and dialysis as technologies for kidney failure, not the kidneys' normal role in filtering urea and balancing water and salts, so it does not teach the same idea at the right depth.

draft.title: The excretory system
card: The kidneys filter the blood. Useful substances such as water and salts are mostly taken back into the blood, and waste is left behind.
a waste made when the body breaks down proteins. The kidneys remove it from the blood and it leaves the body in urine.
the kidneys adjust how much water and salt is returned to the blood. This keeps the amounts in the body steady.
Urine travels from the kidneys through tubes to the bladder, where it is stored until it is released from the body.
draft.remember: Kidneys filter blood: waste leaves in urine, and water and salts are kept in balance.

a.q: Which job do the kidneys do?
opts: Remove urea from blood and balance water and salts
Break down proteins into amino acids for absorption
Store urine until it is released from the body
Make urea from the water and salts in the blood
a.why: The kidneys filter blood, removing urea and adjusting water and salts. Storing urine is tempting, but that is done by the bladder, and urea is made when proteins are broken down, not by the kidneys.
a.clue: Focus on what happens to the blood as it passes through the kidneys.

b.q: Tom drinks a lot of water after a game and his body has more water than it needs. How do his kidneys help restore balance?
opts: They return less water to the blood, so more leaves in urine
They return more water to the blood, so less leaves in urine
They stop filtering the blood until the extra water is used
They turn the extra water into urea to remove it
b.why: The kidneys adjust how much water goes back into the blood. With extra water, less is returned, so more leaves in urine. Returning more water would add to the excess and not restore balance.
b.clue: Extra water needs to leave the body, not stay in the blood.

a.best: Remove urea from blood and balance water and salts

b.best: They return less water to the blood, so more leaves in urine
